Assess signing, provenance, key management and transparency independently, including recovery cost.
Define the acceptance contract and a separate future phase proposal for each selected control.

contracts.title: TDD obligations and phase evidence
requirements: Task tdd objects contain mode and reason; modes are required, not_applicable, or historical, with historical limited to completed F0.
A phase execution record identifies every task, changed files, exact RED/GREEN commits, commands, observed outcomes, refactor notes, and independent review.
The CI validator checks records, file coverage and Git relationships; semantic failure relevance and reviewer identity remain review responsibilities.
Workers retain RED/GREEN checkpoint commits when integrating task branches; no arbitrary evidence command is executed by CI.

decision_gates.topic: Authorized GitHub publication identity
decision_gates.required_decision: Identify and authenticate the authorized bot using existing approved credentials and permissions; never publish using the current personal account.
acceptance: Identity is verifiably the designated bot.
Required publication actions fit its granted repository permissions.
No credentials appear in project artifacts or conversation.

decision_gates.topic: Coverage policy after the first real domain milestone
decision_gates.required_decision: Accepted by the project owner on 2026-10-02 after the genuine M0.04 report: allow at most a 0.25 percentage-point project coverage decrease against the comparison base per PR, with a separate absolute 99% project floor. Retain the 90% patch target with zero tolerance and required critical scenarios. Enforce both project rules through CI / Gate using complete Codecov line reports for the exact event head and base; the current service does not publish the configured project contexts. Keep codecov/patch required from its existing App. Verify hosted enforcement before main integration; no plan upgrade or branch-protection relaxation is required.
acceptance: Use observed coverage behavior and report limits.
Record the selected policy and required contexts without changing it solely to pass a failing change.

decision_gates.topic: Approval binding for implementation-only source changes
decision_gates.required_decision: Define which source and execution/context inputs are covered by an approval, how implementation-only pushes affect proposal revision and consent, and when a previously approved revision becomes ineligible. Preserve exact-source evidence even if consent can remain eligible across an explicitly permitted source change.
acceptance: Examples specify no protected change, changed test content, changed scope/support files, changed governing policy, and changed implementation-only source.
A later push is reassessed and cannot silently reuse evidence from the old source.
A changed covered input creates a new proposal revision requiring fresh exact approval.
The GitHub adapter and promotion coordinator apply the same recorded policy; the candidate cannot weaken it.
M0 remains executable with explicit covered-input bindings and does not assert a selected production rule for this open policy.

decision_gates.topic: Migration tooling and database change discipline
decision_gates.required_decision: Accepted implementation choice on 2026-10-02: Goose v3.28.0 embedded Provider, pgx v5.11.0 and existing sqlc v1.31.1; sequential transactional forward-only migrations with session locking, fresh/repeat/concurrent/populated 1-to-2 upgrade checks, and coordinated A ownership of migrations/query/generator/module files. See ADR 0026 and M1-C01. Real behavior and CI evidence remain required.
acceptance: Fresh-install and supported upgrade scenarios are defined.
Tool choice and migration ownership are versioned.

decision_gates.topic: Runtime configuration and lifecycle
decision_gates.required_decision: Integrator defines trusted configuration/secret sources, process packaging, shutdown and bounded job retry/timeout defaults within the accepted architecture.
acceptance: Secret handling and required settings are explicit.
Restart/shutdown and terminal failure semantics are testable.

decision_gates.topic: Polling targets, budget and MCP boundary
decision_gates.required_decision: Integrator measures feasible repository count/discovery delay and chooses budget, scheduling, coalescing and local MCP schema/auth defaults; escalate only material changes to user-visible guarantees or authority.
acceptance: All trigger paths obey one budget and authenticated GitHub limits.
Discovery after an omitted MCP call, fairness and restart catch-up have measurable tests.
MCP grants only scoped synchronization/status.

decision_gates.topic: Declaration and source-inventory semantics
decision_gates.required_decision: Freeze YAML/path/pattern/case/symlink/submodule and invalid-declaration behavior plus exact identity of approved declaration inputs. The owner decides any material user-facing scope limitation; integrator selects deterministic encoding and parsing.
acceptance: No candidate omission can remove existing protection.
Complete inventory and meaningful configuration changes remain reviewable.
Supported source cases and rejected cases have explicit tests.

decision_gates.topic: GitHub App permissions and supported access
decision_gates.required_decision: Map each operation to minimal GitHub App permissions, supported host and installation/token lifecycle. Preserve outbound-only operation and the already accepted administration capability for confirmed protection setup.
acceptance: Permission matrix covers reads, checks, comments, protection and eventual backup publication without unexplained privileges.
Local/headless access flow works without public webhooks.
Denied/revoked access has a visible scoped state.

decision_gates.topic: Owner identity, policy serialization and credential separation
decision_gates.required_decision: Define initial human proof, local/headless setup sessions, trusted App installation association and explicit SuiteWard authorization; do not infer authority from repository administration. Owner accepts any new authority policy; integrator implements proof and policy encoding.
acceptance: Agent access cannot impersonate the approving owner.
Installation URL parameters alone cannot establish authority.
One eligible owner approval, including own-authored PRs, is preserved.

decision_gates.topic: Effective protection, confirmation and notification lifecycle
decision_gates.required_decision: Integrator selects branch-protection/ruleset APIs, effective-rule comparison, freshness/readback handling and notification identity. Preserve explicit owner confirmation for setup and specific repairs.
acceptance: Preserve unrelated required checks/rules.
Missing/insufficient protection is distinct from unavailable verification.
Material preview changes require new confirmation; detection does not auto-repair.

decision_gates.topic: GitHub check identity and lifecycle
decision_gates.required_decision: Freeze source/context binding, external check-state mapping, stale publication invalidation and truthful notice lifecycle against supported GitHub behavior.
acceptance: Missing approval/incomplete/waiting is never represented by neutral/skipped readiness.
Each source head and changed governing context is reassessed.
Required App source and external presentation are unambiguous.

decision_gates.topic: Priority eligibility and merged-but-unpromotable recovery
decision_gates.required_decision: Integrator designs serialization/generation fencing and deterministic ordering. Owner settles unresolved admission/withdrawal, multiple-suite behavior and recovery when an active merged PR cannot promote; unsupported cases need explicit safe handling.
acceptance: Concurrent commands and delayed writes cannot resurrect obsolete eligibility.
A merged active PR that cannot promote has a usable authorized recovery route.
No automatic priority expiry/reassignment is invented.

decision_gates.topic: Supported GitHub merge contexts and exact integrated source
decision_gates.required_decision: Demonstrate supported merge/squash/rebase/fork/same-SHA/merge-group behavior and exact source resolution. Integrator may restrict technical support only through explicit documented safe behavior; material product limitations go to the owner.
acceptance: Every supported method has real GitHub adapter evidence.
Same-SHA PRs cannot independently claim readiness without proven handling.
A merge in flight during priority transfer is reconciled, not claimed atomically prevented.

decision_gates.topic: Backup format, cryptography, export consistency and capacity
decision_gates.required_decision: Integrator selects a versioned self-contained archive, maintained encryption/compression dependency, consistent export/import method, kit verification/rotation design, size budgets and checkpoint cadence. Preserve all accepted historical content/records and externally held private keys.
acceptance: One snapshot reconstructs every claimed historical version without old commits/archives.
No hashes-only fallback, private recovery key or cross-project data in project archive.
Actual coverage, exact encrypted-byte identity and incomplete state are distinguishable.

decision_gates.topic: Release layout, health clocks and fallback retention
decision_gates.required_decision: Integrator defines Release/tag/asset namespace, verification cadence/budget, capacity and immutable receipt locations. Owner settles escalation after loss of a formerly verified copy and any material retention policy; the 29-day first-coverage rule is already accepted.
acceptance: 29 days measures oldest never-covered recovery-relevant state and survives newer activity/restart.
Fallback/cleanup are reviewable PRs without automatic merge or protection bypass.
Historical referenced bytes remain retrievable and existing product/immutable-release settings are preserved.

decision_gates.topic: Restore compatibility, owner reconnection and instance exclusion
decision_gates.required_decision: Integrator specifies CLI distribution, isolated targets, extraction/format compatibility, progress and operational recredentialing. Owner accepts any new authority policy; loss of owner identity remains unsupported unless separately decided. Choose a verifiable old/new publisher exclusion mechanism. Define how trusted receipt/provenance is obtained and authenticated after loss of the original host, independently of the selected archive; do not select an M3 signing stack implicitly.
acceptance: Offline import never grants current ownership or enables external effects.
Healthy/unrelated project authority cannot be overwritten.
Owner, expected App source, protection and exclusive publisher are verified before resume.
Forged-but-decryptable input is rejected; absent trustworthy provenance remains an explicit recovery condition rather than an authenticity success.

decision_gates.topic: Supported production matrix and license publication
decision_gates.required_decision: Owner confirms supported production/CLI platforms and AGPL only-versus-or-later grant/notices. Integrator chooses packaging and upgrade mechanics within that matrix; native Windows development alone does not imply production Windows support.
acceptance: Clean supported-host install and independent restore drills are reproducible.
Release notices use the accepted grant.
M1 is described as integrity governance, with execution explicitly deferred.

decision_gates.topic: First executable profile and execution trust model
decision_gates.required_decision: M2.01 performs the decision work: choose first ecosystem/RunnerProfile and accepted Docker isolation, resources, network/private dependencies/secrets, trusted observation and supported host guarantees before implementing execution.
acceptance: Known failures/corrections and forged-result cases define acceptance.
No candidate write access to canonical/control state or credentials.
Execution-required assurance cannot silently downgrade when the backend is unavailable.

decision_gates.topic: Future managed execution location and trust
decision_gates.required_decision: Future product decision: provider-hosted execution, customer infrastructure or both, including tenancy/isolation and credential/connectivity responsibilities. This does not block self-hosted M1 or the accepted local Docker backend and has no scheduled implementation task.
acceptance: A future managed proposal names the execution location and threat/operational ownership explicitly.
No current task silently commits to a managed architecture.

decision_gates.topic: Justified future hardening controls
decision_gates.required_decision: M3.01 evaluates concrete threats and proposes controls. The owner chooses justified signing/key-management/provenance/transparency increments; future executable phases are created only after those choices.
acceptance: Each selected control has a concrete threat, independent verification and operating/recovery cost.
No speculative ready M3 implementation tasks or mandatory KMS/OIDC/transparency dependency.
